# Market signals: regulation, insurance and timing

## Regulation sets a date

The EU Machinery Regulation applies in full from January 2027. For operators of connected industrial equipment it requires a documented condition-monitoring process for safety-relevant assets. The VDMA estimates the average compliance gap at 14 months of implementation work, which places the last safe start in late 2025 [Source: VDMA](https://www.vdma.org/maschinenverordnung-umsetzung-2027).

## Insurers price the difference

Two of the three largest industrial insurers in the DACH region introduced condition-monitoring discounts of 8 to 12 percent on business-interruption cover in 2025, and both have announced surcharges for unmonitored critical assets from 2027 [Source: Handelsblatt](https://www.handelsblatt.com/finanzen/versicherungen/industrieversicherer-condition-monitoring-2025). On a 40-asset mid-sized operator the surcharge is estimated at 0.9 million euros over three years.

## Early movers are visible

Operators that started condition-based programmes in 2023 report a 48-to-72-hour detection lead on degradation patterns and a roughly one-third reduction in unnecessary interventions [Source: Fraunhofer IPA](https://www.ipa.fraunhofer.de/de/publikationen/instandhaltung-2025.html). Three years of labelled failure history is the asset competitors cannot buy retroactively [Source: Handelsblatt](https://www.handelsblatt.com/unternehmen/industrie/predictive-maintenance-datenvorsprung-2026).
